# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems will run concurrently throughout the migration. Users are migrated in waves; the old system remains fully operational as a fallback until the new system has proven stable across the entire user base for a defined stabilization period.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — 800 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing (invoicing, payment capture, refunds, tax calculation, and dunning workflows) in staging with zero critical defects, and a rollback procedure has been tested successfully at least once.

- Cohort: internal test accounts plus opted-in low-risk customers (month-to-month, no active disputes, no complex tax jurisdictions).
- Duration: minimum 2 weeks.
- Both systems process in parallel with shadow reconciliation (old system output compared against new system output for every transaction).

## Phase 2: Early Adoption (15% of users — 6,000 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with reconciliation mismatch rate below threshold (see metrics below), no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, and support ticket volume from Phase 1 cohort is within 1.5x baseline.

- Cohort: broader mix including annual-plan customers, but still excluding highest-revenue enterprise accounts.
- Duration: minimum 3 weeks.
- Customer communications sent 7 days ahead of migration per batch.

## Phase 3: General Availability (53% of users — ~21,200 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 metrics hold within threshold for 2 consecutive weeks, finance has signed off on revenue-recognition parity between systems, and on-call/support staffing has been scaled to handle projected ticket volume.

- Cohort: remaining standard and mid-tier accounts.
- Migrated in weekly sub-batches (not all at once) to preserve ability to pause between batches.
- Duration: minimum 4 weeks.

## Phase 4: Final Batch — Complex & Enterprise Accounts (30% of users — 12,000 accounts)
**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 fully complete with cumulative reconciliation error rate below threshold, zero open Sev-1 incidents, and dedicated migration runbooks reviewed with each enterprise account's assigned CSM.

- Cohort: highest-revenue, custom-contract, multi-entity, and complex-tax accounts requiring white-glove handling.
- Migrated in small named batches with a dedicated support bridge during each batch's cutover window.
- **Note:** The legacy system is NOT decommissioned in this phase. It remains live in read-only/fallback mode through a separate Phase 5 (post-migration stabilization), decoupled from any user-migration activity.

## Phase 5: Legacy Decommission (0% of users — infrastructure only)
**Entry criterion:** 100% of users successfully migrated and stable on new system for a minimum 30-day stabilization window with no rollback events, all historical data reconciled and archived, and finance/audit sign-off obtained.

- This phase involves no user migration — only decommissioning of the old billing system (data archival, access revocation, infrastructure teardown).

---

## Halt/Rollback Metrics

- **Reconciliation mismatch rate ≥ 0.5%** of transactions in any 24-hour window during a phase → halt further migrations in that phase pending root-cause analysis.
- **Payment failure rate increase of more than 20% relative** to the pre-migration baseline for a migrated cohort, sustained over 2 hours → halt and investigate.
- **Support ticket volume exceeding 2x baseline** for a migrated cohort within 48 hours of a batch cutover → pause the next scheduled batch.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or missed charges due to both systems processing the same invoice | Implement idempotency keys and a real-time reconciliation job that flags any invoice processed by both systems within the same billing cycle | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors (tax codes, currency, payment tokens) causing incorrect customer charges | Run automated field-by-field validation against a schema contract before each batch cutover, with manual spot-checks on a 5% sample | Data Migration Lead
RISK: Customer confusion or churn from unexpected billing changes | Send advance notice emails per batch, provide a dedicated support channel, and offer a grace-period credit for billing errors introduced by migration | Customer Success Lead
RISK: Payment gateway/token incompatibility between old and new systems causing failed transactions | Pre-validate stored payment methods against the new gateway in a sandbox pass before each batch, and maintain fallback routing to the old system for failed tokens | Payments Engineering Lead
RISK: Rollback of a batch after cutover causes data loss or double billing | Maintain a frozen snapshot of pre-migration state per batch and a tested rollback runbook with a defined maximum rollback window (e.g., 72 hours) | SRE/Platform Lead

PHASES: 5
